newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU institutions urged to have openess rules.
newsitem.headline: EU institutions urged to have openess rules.

text.p: The European Union's ombudsman Jacob Soderman has told a string of EU institutions to adopt openness rules like those in place in the European Commission and Council of Ministers.
Soderman -- in his first own initiative action since becoming the EU watchdog -- said they should adopt rules on public access to documents.
"Failure to adopt such rules is maladministration," he said in a statement.
Among the organisations concerned are the European Parliament, the European Court of Justice and the European Monetary Institute.
He said the rules should apply to all documents, except those already covered by existing legal provisions allowing access or requiring confidentiality.
He gave the institutions concerned three months to respond.
He said that in the case of the Court of Justice, the European Parliament and the European Monetary Institute the recommendations should only apply to administrative documents.
